title: Marianne Brandt, tea infuser MT 49
lede: A small metal teapot composed of a hemisphere, a disc, a cylinder, and a half-circle handle on a cross-shaped foot.
summary: Hemisphere body, flat cylindrical lid, half-disc ebony handle, cross foot. Marianne Brandt, Bauhaus metal workshop, 1924.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected Lucia Moholy’s 1924 photograph of the infuser on the Bauhaus Kooperation page, in the scratchpad only. The Met record gives materials and dimensions.

styles.note: A key object of the Bauhaus metal workshop: elementary solids and a half-circle handle, with no ornament.

context: Bauhaus Kooperation says Brandt made the infuser in her first year of study, 1924, in the metal workshop under László Moholy-Nagy, and that the Bauhaus often criticized the use of costly materials such as silver and ebony. [Bauhaus Kooperation](https://bauhauskooperation.de/wissen/das-bauhaus/werke/metall/tee-extraktkaennchen-mt-49).
The Met holds an example: “Tea Infuser and Strainer,” ca. 1924, silver and ebony, 8.3 × 10.8 × 16.5 cm, accession 2000.63a–c. [The Met 491299](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/491299).
observed: The body is a polished metal hemisphere that reflects its surroundings.
A flat disc lid sits on a short cylinder; a small black cylindrical knob sits on top.
The handle is a flat black half-disc, fixed to the body with a rectangular bracket.
A short straight spout projects at left.
The body rests on a small crossed foot.
interpretation: The infuser shows the Bauhaus approach to form in three dimensions: each part is one elementary solid, and the parts meet without transitions. It is the object equivalent of circles and bars in a poster.
borrow: Build a component from separate elementary shapes and keep the joins visible.
Contrast one polished or bright material with one flat black part.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Bauhaus Kooperation credits its photograph “Bauhaus-Archiv Berlin / © VG Bild-Kunst, Bonn.” The Met marks its record as not public domain. Brandt died in 1983 or 1984 (sources differ).
